finding.claim: wipe() never enforces the OWNER role: requireRole() returns a boolean that is discarded, so any authenticated User, regardless of roles, can reach repo.wipe(tenant), a destructive tenant-wipe operation.
finding.source: Caller-supplied User u (roles Set<String>) and tenant String from POST /tenants/{t}/wipe (comment at line 24). Attacker needs only a valid authenticated session with any role or an empty role set.
finding.sink: repo.wipe(tenant) at Admin.java:27 (destructive, irreversible tenant deletion)

trace.note: Route comment: POST /tenants/{t}/wipe, tenant is path-controlled
wipe(User u, String tenant) entry point; u and tenant are not validated here
requireRole(u, "OWNER") called as a bare statement; return value discarded, so no check happens
requireRole returns u.roles().contains(role) and does not throw (per its doc comment at line 13), so there is no side-effect enforcement

finding.guards_checked: requireRole at lines 14-16: boolean-returning, no throw, result unused at call site, so no effective guard. No other check in wipe(). Contrast export() at lines 31-33, which uses checkRole (throws SecurityException) and is correctly gated. No authentication or routing filter is in this repo to check upstream; if one exists it must enforce OWNER for this route, which cannot be verified from this file.
finding.repro: Authenticated user with roles = Set.of() (or Set.of("VIEWER")) calls admin.wipe(new User("x", Set.of()), "victimTenant"). requireRole returns false, nothing is thrown, repo.wipe("victimTenant") runs.

verdict.guard_found: None effective. requireRole (src/Admin.java:14-16) returns a boolean and does not throw, and its result is discarded as a bare statement at src/Admin.java:26. No other check precedes repo.wipe(tenant) at src/Admin.java:27. The throwing variant checkRole (lines 18-22) is used only by export() at line 32, not wipe().
verdict.reason: wipe() at src/Admin.java:26 calls requireRole, which returns a boolean (src/Admin.java:14-15) that is discarded, so repo.wipe(tenant) at line 27 runs for any caller with a User object, regardless of roles. The trace matches the code. The one caveat is that route-level authentication or authorization is not in this repo, so an upstream filter enforcing OWNER could block it. That filter cannot be checked from this code, but the method itself enforces nothing.

finding.claim: Neither wipe() nor export() checks that the caller is authorized for the specific tenant. User carries only global roles, so an OWNER of one tenant can wipe or export any other tenant (broken object-level authorization / IDOR).
finding.source: Tenant string from the path parameter {t} (line 24, 30); caller User u with a global roles Set (line 4), which has no tenant field.
finding.sink: repo.wipe(tenant) at Admin.java:27 and repo.export(tenant) at Admin.java:33 (cross-tenant data export and destructive wipe)

trace.note: User record has roles only, no tenant or membership attribute
export(User u, String tenant) entry point
checkRole(u, "OWNER") verifies a global role only; it does not compare tenant to u's tenants
repo.export(tenant) runs for any tenant string supplied by the caller
Same pattern in wipe(): tenant is never bound to u

finding.guards_checked: checkRole (lines 18-22) for export only checks the global role. No tenant-membership check exists in this file for either method. Whether the tenant scope is enforced upstream (e.g., roles resolved per tenant before this call, or a tenant-scoped Repo) cannot be confirmed from this file. Medium confidence until the caller and Repo implementation are reviewed.
finding.repro: User u = new User("a", Set.of("OWNER")) belonging to tenant A. admin.export(u, "tenantB") passes checkRole and calls repo.export("tenantB"), exporting another tenant's data.

verdict.guard_found: For export: checkRole (src/Admin.java:18-22) checks only the global role and throws, so it blocks non-OWNER callers but not cross-tenant access. For wipe: requireRole (src/Admin.java:14-16) returns a bool, and the call at line 26 discards it, so it is no guard at all. No tenant-membership check exists anywhere in src/Admin.java for either method.
verdict.reason: wipe() at src/Admin.java:25-27 has no effective check because requireRole's bool result is discarded at line 26, so any caller can wipe any tenant; export() at lines 31-33 checks only the global role via checkRole (line 32) and never binds tenant to u, so an OWNER can export another tenant's data, and the file gives User no tenant attribute that could enforce scope. The export IDOR depends on whether OWNER is meant to be tenant-scoped, which this file cannot settle, but the wipe defect stands on its own.
